records.description:
# Petros Pizanias

Ionian University, History, Emeritus

Petros Th. Pizanias is Emeritus Professor of History, Department of History, Ionian University. He studied history at École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales and has worked as a Visiting Professor in several French universities. He directed the Post-Graduate Studies program, Department of History, and held the UNESCO chair for the training on teaching and researching history in the Balkans. He has published extensively in journals, such as Annales ESC, and Ta Istorika, he has organized international conferences, and has published nine books in the field of Modern and Contemporary Greek History. His most recent books include The Greek Revolutionof 1821: A European Event, Isis publications, and the proposed book published in Greek by Hestia Publications. He was also the chairman of the scientific committee of the Institute of Strategic and Development Studies – A. Papandreou, and advisor to the Minister of National Education (1997-1999). Since 2001, he has been the Principal Investigator of a historical research titled "The Hermes of Modern Greeks" a digital database with prosopographical parameters of selected social groups which played an important role in the 1821 Greek revolution. He is currently completing a book on the general history of the 1821 Greek revolution.Curriculum Vitae: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petros_PizaniasE-mail: [email protected] Address: Abati 5, 11741 Athens, Greece

15 pages

## Abstract

Licencias de saca de lana in Archivo General de Simancas it is made a research to analyze wool trade in Castille at the end of 16th century. records.title: (PDF) MIHAJLOVIC RIDELLA 2021 Notes on Ragusan Ships and Men in Spanish service
records.description: Numerous Ragusan ships and men were engaged in three Spanish war campaigns during the 1580s. During an audience with the Spanish Viceroy in Naples in August 1581, the Ragusan envoy stated that as many as 35 Ragusan navi were engaged in the Portugal campaign, which took place in 1580. Large Ragusan ships were also involved in the subsequent Azores campaigns, which took place from 1581 to 1583. Seven Arragucesas were a part of the 1583 fleet of Marquis of Santa Cruz. Their tonnage constituted one-fourth of the overall tonnage, excluding galleys and smaller vessels. In both events they served as troop and supplies carriers and did not directly participate in the actual combat. One vessel, the San Nicolò, captained by Marino Prodanelli, participated in the Azores campaigns during 1582 and 1583, as well as in the Levantine squadron of the Spanish Armada of 1588. Other Ragusan ships in the Armada of 1588 were Santa Maria della Grazia e San Giovanni Battista, Santa Annunziata and Santa Maria del Bissone. All perished during the campaign.

records.title: (PDF) Leiden – Petrus Bloccius and Jan van Hout
records.description: Introduction to the Reformation in Leiden: The early printing of Lutheran books, lutherizing priests, and the Leiden Anabaptists. The development of an early Reformed group is illustrated in the life of Petrus Bloccius, a humanist scholar and the conrector of the city’s Latin school. The later developments can be illustrated by the influential town secretary Jan van Hout (1542-1609). The disputes between the magistracy and the Reformed Church about their conflicting Reformed views of church government were settled at the end of the 1580s and a multi-denominational society developed.

records.title: (PDF) Bishops and Politics: The Portuguese Episcopacy during the Dynastic Crisis of 1580
records.description:
## Abstract

Using Pierre Bourdieu's concept of "field", this essay assumes that there was no single "Church position" during Portugal's dynastic crisis of 1578-81: Portugal's Church was an institution encompassing a large number of different agencies, each containing a huge number of very different agents (from a social, cultural, economic and even religious perspective) struggling for power and influence and disputing control over material, spiritual and symbolic goods. Therefore, my purpose is to explain the various and changing ways that the different prelates of Portugal's thirteen mainland dioceses responded to the acute political problem of the royal succession between 1578 and 1581, and how the crown candidates tried to obtain their support. Church History, Bishops, Portuguese dynastic crisis of 1580, Political history, Religious 'field' Partindo do conceito de "campo" tal como formulado por Pierre Bourdieu, este estudo assume que não existiu uma posição unitária da Igreja no agitado processo político que marcou a vida portuguesa nos anos da crise dinástica (1578)(1579)(1580)(1581). A Igreja portuguesa era uma instituição constituída por várias instâncias e organismos, englobando diferentes agentes, tanto do ponto de vista social, como económico, cultural e até religioso, os quais lutavam por poder e influência e disputavam a posse de bens materiais, espirituais e simbólicos. Em face desta perspectiva, a intenção central da análise aqui apresentada é explicar como é que cada um dos bispos que ocuparam as 13 dioceses do reino de Portugal se posicionaram e actuaram no contexto da vida política portuguesa, entre 1578 e 1581, e como é que os candidatos à sucessão da Coroa portuguesa em 1580 tentaram obter o seu apoio Pa l a v r a s-ch a v e História da Igreja; Bispos; União Ibérica; História político-religiosa; Campo religioso * I wish to thank my friend and American colleague William Monter for his assistance in improving the English of my original draft.
